solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hobnail safe when hammered in

indicators.note: metal that is hammered is beaten out of its old shape into a new one

blocks.note: taken as written, all eleven letters

explanation.surface: A cobbler or locksmith driving hobnails into a safe door.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last little word: 'in' as an adjective, as in 'the in thing'. A hobnail is a heavy nail for boot soles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as in is currently popular and in style, so the adjective is a casual synonym.

clue.text: Mark European post with colours?

blocks.note: to flag something is to mark it for attention
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone marking a European letter with coloured pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail, and 'colours' like crayons; here the post is an upright pole and the colours are a flag, as in a regiment's colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's or ship's colours are its flag, and the tall upright pole from which they fly is this.

clue.text: Plant put on pebble

blocks.note: to put on a show is to sham, to pretend
a pebble is a small rock

explanation.surface: An instruction to set a potted plant on top of a pebble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' reads as placing one thing on another, but it means to feign.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a small clover, the three-leaved national emblem of Ireland, so a plant by example.

clue.text: Matter found in napkin, perhaps, when surface cleared

indicators.note: clearing the surface strips off the top layer, so the front of the word goes

blocks.note: a paper napkin is one kind of tissue

explanation.surface: Something spotted in a napkin once the table has been wiped.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the surface is the top, so clearing it loses the first letter T. 'Perhaps' warns that a napkin is only an example of a tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under discussion is an issue: both mean a subject or topic of concern.

clue.text: Most curious where one sits when relocated

indicators.note: things relocated are moved elsewhere, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prying person wondering where they will be seated after a move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where one sits' sounds like a seat, but only 'one sits' is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nosy means prying and inquisitive, so the superlative of nosy matches the most curious person.

clue.text: Offer impressing leader in gaslighter, that man a narcissist

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted
to impress is to press into, so the outer word takes the others inside it

blocks.note: a bid is an offer at auction
the opening letter of the word
the pronoun for a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A manipulative partner who is also a narcissist being offered something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaslighter' and 'narcissist' paint a toxic partner, but the first only lends its opening letter; 'a' is not part of the definition but goes inside with the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bighead is a conceited person who boasts about themselves, close in sense to a self-admiring narcissist.

clue.text: Funny girl then, a human

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that a comic girl turned out to be a person after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny Girl' looks like the musical title; 'Funny' is the anagram signal and 'girl then, a' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction calls an inhabitant of planet Earth an earthling, which is exactly what a person is.

clue.text: Cut identified

blocks.note: first meaning: to cut with a toothed blade
second meaning: past tense of see, noticed or recognised

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate meanings: a verb for cutting wood and the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to cut timber with a toothed tool, and it is also the past tense of see, meaning spotted or recognised.

clue.text: Adagio, where bass appears in secret

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be found inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a bass note is a low one
sly means stealthy or secretive

explanation.surface: A musical slow movement in which a secret bass line is hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'bass' look like an instrument; it simply means low.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the Italian tempo marking telling players to perform at a slow, leisurely pace.

clue.text: It’s amazing hugging diseased tree

indicators.note: a hug wraps arms around someone, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the exclamation someone makes at something amazing
diseased means sick

explanation.surface: A tree-hugger marvelling at a sick tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's amazing' stands for an exclamation, the sound you make at something amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: The willow is a common waterside tree, often weeping, so it is a tree by example.

clue.text: Gather some moss, a majority rolled over

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters sit within the phrase
a thing rolled over ends up facing the other way

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A nod to the proverb about a rolling stone gathering no moss.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a rolling stone gathers no moss; here 'rolled over' tells you to read the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a quantity over time, matching gather as a verb.

clue.text: Predatory bird after grub, as flying — something sweet in that

indicators.note: flying things scatter in all directions, so the letters are thrown about
after places one piece behind the rest in reading order

blocks.note: taken as written
an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: An owl swooping on a grub while something sweet waits in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer as the container for something sweet: a vessel with sugar in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar bowl is the table dish that holds sweetener, so it is a thing with something sweet inside.

clue.text: By grave, keep going

blocks.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
a grave situation is a severe one

explanation.surface: Mourners standing at a graveside told to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place, but it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to continue steadily despite difficulty, the same as carrying on or keeping going.

clue.text: Nothing beyond infernal world — what do we have here then?

definitions.text: what do we have here then?

indicators.note: beyond means further along, so this piece follows the next one

blocks.note: the underworld of the damned
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A visitor peering past the underworld and asking what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase of surprise; the word is used in that sense, like a policeman's 'Hello, hello, what's all this?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Said with raised eyebrows, the greeting doubles as an exclamation of surprise at finding something unexpected.

clue.text: Exclusion by management when hair revealed

blocks.note: a lock is a tress of hair
a secret that is out has been revealed

explanation.surface: A dress code row: staff barred by bosses after showing their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the industrial-relations sense, not a lost key.
explanation.definitionFit: In a labour dispute employers may shut workers out of the workplace, an exclusion imposed by the employer.

clue.text: Nothing very rash, yet remarkably rash!

definitions.note: the final word is the definition; the first 'rash' is fodder

indicators.note: remarkably means in a striking, unusual way, so the letters turn out unusually arranged

blocks.note: O looks like zero
V is the standard abbreviation for very
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox: something that is not reckless at all, yet startlingly reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'rash' appears twice: first as raw letters, then as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overhasty means acting too quickly without due thought, which is what being rash is.

clue.text: Kill noise, hullabaloo finally muffled

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter counts
a muffled thing is wrapped up inside something, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to silence a racket and a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kill noise' reads as one instruction to silence it; 'Kill' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Do in is informal British slang for murder or finish off, a phrasal verb meaning to kill.

clue.text: Diversion of road with loco in US river

indicators.note: a diversion sends traffic off its usual route, so the letters take a new course

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road and railway being rerouted around an American river.
explanation.walkthrough: A diversion is the British word for a detour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado is the major American river that carved out the Grand Canyon.

clue.text: Nurse brought in a letter for visitor

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so it is placed within another piece

blocks.note: to nurse a patient is to tend them
A, plus TEE, the spelt-out name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A nurse admitted to deliver a letter for a hospital visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A letter' is not mail: it is A plus the name of a letter spelt out, TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends an event or meeting comes along as a guest, so they are a visitor.

clue.text: Considered material

blocks.note: first meaning: believed or judged
second meaning: a matted woollen fabric

explanation.walkthrough: 'Considered material' reads as carefully thought-out content; split it into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of feel, meaning judged or believed, and also names a pressed wool fabric.

clue.text: Four involved in ordeal — hardly worth mentioning?

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it

blocks.note: Roman numeral four
a trial is a painful ordeal

explanation.surface: Four people caught up in a gruelling experience that they then play down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is so minor or unimportant that it scarcely deserves a remark.

clue.text: This vessel’s small and powerful, but has got a failing

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so the letters fall apart and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A compact, mighty boat that nonetheless has a weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' reads as a noun, a flaw, but it is the anagram signal working on the words just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tugs are compact harbour boats with very strong engines, used to push and tow much larger ships.

clue.text: Cross with Gael, not furious

indicators.note: furious suggests wild, violent agitation, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed with a Scot or Irishman, though not raging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' and 'not furious' look like matching moods; 'Cross' is a hybrid and 'furious' is the anagram signal. A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Scot or Irish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid bred from tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit, so it is a botanical cross.

clue.text: Expression of disappointment is awful where hospital closed off

indicators.note: something closed off is shut in, enclosed by what surrounds it

blocks.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
slang: it sucks means it is awful

explanation.surface: A complaint that a local hospital being shut down is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hospital closed off' reads like a ward closure; here the hospital letter is enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shucks is a mild American exclamation of regret or embarrassment, said when things go slightly wrong.

clue.text: Superior dirty clothes ending in bin

indicators.note: the ending is the final part, so only the closing letter is used
to clothe is to cover or wrap, so one piece is dressed around another

blocks.note: covered in soot, grimy
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A haughty person dumping filthy clothes in the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun for garments; it is the verb, to clothe, wrapping one piece round another.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooty person acts superior, treating others with haughty disdain and condescension.

clue.text: Theory in truth unchallenged

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the word break

explanation.surface: A theory that turns out to be true and goes undisputed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunch is an intuitive guess or unproven idea, a loose sense of the word theory.

clue.text: Something afoot, seemingly — as private person mentioned?

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so it counts by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: private feelings are inner ones
a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'

explanation.surface: A suspicion that a secretive individual is up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afoot' usually means happening, but here it literally means inside a shoe, at the foot. An inner soul is one's private self.
explanation.definitionFit: This lining insert sits inside a shoe under the foot, so it is literally something placed at the foot.

clue.text: Problem ending in tears, especially when upset

indicators.note: the ending is the final part, so only the closing letter is used
upset means knocked over, and in a down clue that turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: the closing letter of the word
uber, from German, is a prefix meaning especially or super, as in uber-cool

explanation.surface: A personal problem that ends in tears, particularly when someone is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like distress; it turns the whole thing upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle in which images and letters stand for words, a kind of problem to solve.

clue.text: Waspish given sack — hostile exchange

blocks.note: waspish means irritable, bad-tempered
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: An irritable employee is sacked and a bitter row follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given sack' reads as being dismissed; 'given' merely joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is gunfire from two directions, used figuratively for an angry argument with remarks flying both ways.

clue.text: Panel twiddling thumbs when in conference?

indicators.note: a conference is a spoken discussion, so the word counts by how it is heard

blocks.note: people twiddling their thumbs have nothing to do and are fed up

explanation.surface: Members of a committee idly fidgeting through a long meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In conference' fits a meeting of the panel, but it means 'when spoken'.
explanation.definitionFit: A board of directors or examiners is a group of people who decide things together, like a panel.

clue.text: Right to an opinion, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: a chance to give a view
second meaning: used to introduce an instance

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a phrase about free speech; split it before 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a voice in a decision is having a say, and the word also introduces an illustration, like e.g.

clue.text: US river, wet and grey

blocks.note: wet means feeble and spineless, and yellow means cowardly
stone is a pale greyish colour

explanation.surface: A dreary description of an American river on a rainy day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British slang for weak or wimpy, so it stands for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yellowstone is a long American river flowing through the national park of the same name.
